writing.rule: An error should identify the operation without copying credentials into logs.
writing.explanation:
A bare connection failed message loses the operation and request that failed. Add bounded structured context: operation name, request ID and a stable error category. Keep secret fields out of the event. Redacting only one capitalization of Authorization is insufficient when headers are case insensitive.

This lab preserves field order while replacing authorization, cookie, password, token and api_key values with [REDACTED], case insensitively. It does not claim that this small allowlist finds every possible secret in free text. Production code should prefer explicitly selected safe fields and never dump arbitrary request bodies or connection URLs. Diagnostic context is useful only when a person can connect it to a specific operation; a giant unstructured debug print can be harder to use than a short event with a correlation ID.

The route project is Task Ledger: first keep a reproducible source history, then expose its data through a CLI and HTTP boundary, persist it in SQL, diagnose failures and prepare a release. This lesson owns one contract in that project. Run the worked example before changing the starter and explain which input makes the tempting shortcut fail.

Terminal practice: Run the companion error case and inspect its request ID and operation context. Keep Authorization out of retained terminal command examples.

The compiler lab is independent of the reading question. Edit solution.rs; the app supplies a separate caller with normal, empty and adversarial inputs. A successful unchanged demonstration does not prove your implementation. After the lab, apply the same contract to the route companion project. Its README separates the on-device adapter from the desktop Cargo/TCP profile.
